title: NebulaScale - marketplace packaging & edge connectivity ops sync
summary: Partner sync to align on Azure/GCP marketplace packaging, private VPC edge connector patterns, AMI vs container listing options, billing hooks and security artifacts. Agreed pilot test plan and deliverables for package, terraform module, and security checklist.
topics: marketplace packaging options (container image vs AMI)
billing and metering hooks for marketplace
deployment tests and CI to validate listing readiness
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arun (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Jenna (NebulaScale PM), Hugo (NebulaScale Cloud Arch), Lisa (NebulaScale Marketplace Ops), Marcus (NebulaScale DevOps)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Discussed packaging approach for Azure and GCP marketplace listing; tradeoffs between AMI/VM image and container offering; connectivity patterns for edge customers requiring VPC peering or on-prem connectors; audit and encryption (KMS) questions; agreed next steps to exchange a draft marketplace package and run a staging deploy.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we tried to keep to an hour but we've got 52 minutes in the calendar so let's run through agenda.
[00:10] Jenna Morales: hey thanks Maya, appreciate it. Quick note, Lisa's gonna focus on the listing artifacts, Marcus will cover what's already in our CI.
[00:18] Arun Patel: cool, i'll start with a quick recap of the options — container image listing vs VM/AMI, and then show the edge connector reference arch we've been iterating on.
[00:27] Dr. Hugo Tan: sounds good. we have a handful of regulated customers that need either private VPC deploys or a lightweight on-prem agent, so connectivity and audit logs are the priority.

[00:45] Arun Patel: ok, container-based listing is typically faster for us to onboard, supports autoscaling in the cloud, and is compatible with our dedicated + private runtimes. the AMI/VM path is heavier but sometimes required for customers who want full air-gapped installs. note: we've seen mis-reads in some marketplace requirements where the AMI has to include licensing components — so that's a manual step.
[01:12] Marcus Liu: yeah, and our existing terraform modules expect images as containers; we'd need to add Packer/AMI build pipelines if we go that route. right now we have a registry and cloudbuild pipeline.
[01:28] Sofia Alvarez: one quick imperfect transcript note — sometimes the doc generator mislabels KV cache as "K V cash" in the doc, so we'll send the clean copy.

[01:40] Jenna Morales: biggest question for us — can Redwood support both a marketplace "SaaS listing" that points at hosted Redwood API and a "bring-your-own" listing that triggers a Dedicated/Private deploy? some of our customers want a single-button marketplace launch that provisions a private VPC.
[02:05] Maya Chen: yes, we can. typical pattern is marketplace purchases create a provisioning ticket in our provisioning system and either route to Hosted (fast) or spin up Dedicated/Private images per customer. for private deploys we rely on the partner's infra templates — so we need the terraform module and cloud-init scripts.
[02:24] Lisa Park: for marketplace compliance we also need signed artifacts and a reproducible build. what's Redwood's approach on artifact signing and KMS integration?
[02:36] Arun Patel: we support KMS encryption for customer keys; for signing images we recommend PGP signatures and a reproducible build step. for private deployments we integrate with customer's KMS via IAM roles or cross-account KMS grants. note: sometimes the marketplace wants an SBOM, that is software bill-of-materials, and that's usually a separate deliverable.
[02:58] Dr. Hugo Tan: SBOM is non-negotiable for some customers. we also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM — do you support pushing logs to partner endpoints or do we pull from Redwood?
[03:12] Maya Chen: Redwood can export audit logs via S3 or streaming to partners' Kafka/Cloud PubSub endpoints; for Private customers it's usually dual-write (local logs + central telemetry). for hosted customers we retain audit signals per SLA and can produce syslog exports.

[03:34] Jenna Morales: okay great. next — networking. our spec wants either a VPC peering model, a VPN tunnel, or a light agent that sits in the customer's subnet. which pattern do you prefer?
[03:47] Arun Patel: for latency-sensitive workloads we prefer VPC peering when in same cloud region. for customers with strict network boundaries we use a site-to-site VPN terminated on a bastion host and the edge connector handles KV cache sync. the lightweight agent is good for air-gapped sites — it only requires egress to our control plane via an outbound tunnel, but the agent must be explicitly approved in the customer's hardened baseline.
[04:16] Marcus Liu: that outbound-only model is useful. our security team prefers outbound-only egress to avoid inbound firewall rules. how does the key rotation happen if the agent stores tokens?
[04:28] Sofia Alvarez: we use short-lived tokens and retrieve via a mutual TLS handshake to KMS-backed auth service; rotation can be automated via the agent's built-in renewal flow every 12 hours (configurable).

[04:45] [Customer side cross-talk] Lisa Park: -- can you send the agent spec? -- yes, we'll attach it.

[05:02] Arun Patel: i'm going to share the reference arch doc after this call. little caveat: some of the diagrams use internal names like "redwood-edge-connector", transcription sometimes renders as "red wood edge conner" so ignore that.

[05:18] Maya Chen: on the marketplace listing metadata — pricing hooks. NebulaScale wants metered billing based on concurrent sessions + token usage. marketplaces often allow metered billing but the payload differs per provider. do you have a preferred metering model?
[05:36] Jenna Morales: yes, our marketplace supports metered SKU with hourly metering, and we can pass usage reports back to Redwood. we need the event schema for usage though.
[05:47] Arun Patel: we'll provide a usage schema — top-level fields: customer_id, timestamp, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, concurrent_sessions. FYI transcription glitch: tokens_in was sometimes transcribed as "tockens in" earlier in our docs.

[06:03] Dr. Hugo Tan: about model pinning and rollouts: how do we ensure versioning compatibility for private deploys? some of our customers want to pin to a quantized variant.
[06:15] Maya Chen: Redwood supports model version pinning per deployment; the private control plane includes a model repo and you can choose to deploy a quantized variant. we'll surface compatibility matrix in the release notes. note: we recommend validating on a staging cluster with a sample promptset before production rollout.

[06:39] Marcus Liu: can we run a smoke benchmark? we'd like a 95th percentile latency target and token throughput tests from our region to the deployed instance.
[06:49] Arun Patel: absolutely, we can run a benchmark harness. our usual checklist: (1) synthetic token throughput test, (2) end-to-end prompt set (customer supplied), (3) KV cache warm/cold scenarios. we'll schedule a bench run in the staging env.

[07:08] Lisa Park: for listing requirements — do you have a manifest template? marketplaces often want a YAML manifest plus screenshots and a test account.
[07:18] Sofia Alvarez: yes, we have a marketplace manifest template (we'll share). it includes fields for SSO, privacy policy link, docs, package checksum, and a test endpoint. screenshots are optional but helpful.

[07:34] [08:00] Jenna Morales: about SSO — customers want SAML and OIDC. do you support both?
[08:06] Maya Chen: we support SAML and OIDC for enterprise customers; for marketplace quickstarts we can include an initial test user and then customers can setup SSO post-provisioning.

[08:24] Dr. Hugo Tan: security review time — will Redwood provide SOC2-type artifacts or a security questionnaire for the marketplace?
[08:33] Maya Chen: yes we'll provide SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary, and a standard security questionnaire. sometimes the marketplace requires the partner to supply specific attestation and any localized regulations; we'll fill those sections.

[08:52] Marcus Liu: regarding observability, we need distributed tracing context. do you propagate trace IDs through the model inference pipeline?
[09:01] Arun Patel: yes, we propagate trace IDs and surface per-request traces in the control plane. we can forward spans to partner tracing backends or provide a trace export. small note: sample span field names in our docs may be mis-typed by the transcript generator.

[09:20] Jenna Morales: timeline/next steps? we want a pilot deploy in our staging marketplace environment within two weeks if possible.
[09:28] Maya Chen: two weeks is tight but doable. proposed milestones: day 0-3 exchange artifacts and manifest, day 4-7 Redwood produces a staging package + terraform module, day 8-12 partner runs staging deploy and we run bench tests, day 13-14 iterate and sign off.

[09:50] Lisa Park: are there blockers on your side for providing the package? we have legal review windows for the listing so earlier is better.

[10:00] Sofia Alvarez: the main blocker is getting NebulaScale's required metering schema and the SSO metadata for test accounts. also if you choose AMI route we'll need the Packer pipeline access.

[10:16] [11:00] Jenna Morales: we can provide SSO metadata and the metering fields by EOD tomorrow. Marcus will coordinate CI access for the AMI builds if needed.

[11:22] Arun Patel: technical detail — for image signing we recommend the output be a sha256 checksum plus a PGP signature; we can consume either from an S3 URL or a verified container registry manifest.

[11:36] Dr. Hugo Tan: anything special for on-prem? memory footprint constraints? some of our edge customers only allow 8 vCPU / 32GB RAM boxes.
[11:47] Maya Chen: yes we have a lightweight quantized model that runs within 8 vCPU/32GB but with degraded peak throughput. we'll share the quantized profile matrix with expected latency numbers.

[12:05] Marcus Liu: will the private deployment include automatic patching? some customers expect security updates automated.
[12:15] Sofia Alvarez: patching strategy is configurable — we can enable automated security patch rollouts or manual patch windows per customer SLA. marketplace deployments often default to manual so partners can certify.

[12:34] [12:45] Jenna Morales: ok can we talk about required test accounts, cause the marketplace wants a test buyer flow to validate purchase + provisioning.
[12:55] Maya Chen: we'll provide a test buyer script and webhook consumer for the provisioning flow. important: the webhook must be secured with signed secrets; we'll include an example verification patch.

[13:18] [13:45] Lisa Park: question on billing reconciliation: how do we validate metered usage against marketplace reports?
[13:53] Arun Patel: we recommend a reconciliation run weekly where Redwood sends usage CSV and the partner/marketplace matches the events. we also store raw event payloads for 90 days by default. if you need longer retention we can increase with an add-on.

[14:12] Dr. Hugo Tan: for VPC peering are there egress cost concerns crossing accounts or cloud regions?
[14:23] Maya Chen: yes egress cost varies by provider; for high-throughput customers we recommend collocated deployments (same region) or Dedicated pools to avoid cross-region egress. we'll include cost guidance in the reference arch doc.

[14:41] Marcus Liu: can you share the sample terraform module? we want to adapt it to our infra.
[14:48] Sofia Alvarez: we'll push a sample module repo with variables for region, instance_type, and image_source (container vs ami).

[15:02] [15:30] Jenna Morales: on the legal side, marketplace requires indemnity liabilities in the listing. will Redwood sign standard partner terms?
[15:40] Maya Chen: Redwood uses a partner addendum for marketplace listings; legal will review but we typically accept marketplace standard terms with a data-processing addendum for customer data.

[15:55] Lisa Park: any known blockers for the pilot?
[16:02] Arun Patel: only blockers i see: (1) receive metering schema, (2) SSO test metadata, (3) decide container vs AMI for the pilot. if we choose container we can accelerate.

[16:18] Dr. Hugo Tan: let's go container for the pilot and iterate AMI later. Hugo: plus we need the SBOM and signed manifest.

[16:30] Maya Chen: perfect — container pilot it is. we'll scope the staging package for container image with terraform module and a small agent sample for the outbound-only connectivity.

[16:46] Sofia Alvarez: quick FYI: some marketplaces require screenshots or a demo video — we can record a 2-minute deploy + smoke test clip and attach.

[17:00] Jenna Morales: that helps. timeline check again?
[17:06] Maya Chen: restating milestones in plain language: tomorrow (EOD) NebulaScale provides metering schema + SSO metadata; by 2026-02-09 Redwood sends staging package and terraform module; week of 2026-02-10 partner runs staging deploy and we schedule benchmark run; 2026-02-15 iterate and aim to approve listing for marketplace staging.

[17:36] [Wrap-up cross-talk] Marcus Liu: i'll open an internal ticket for CI access.

[17:50] Maya Chen: ok let's assign action items and close out. thanks everyone.

[18:00] End of recording (approx).

Notes on transcript quality: Automatic transcription occasionally garbles product names (example: "redwood-edge-connector" -> "red wood edge conner"), and some technical acronyms like SBOM, AMI are sometimes expanded or spelled out wrong.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share draft marketplace manifest template and sample terraform module (staging) by 2026-02-09
Jenna Morales: Provide metering schema and SSO/OIDC & SAML test metadata by 2026-02-05 (EOD)
Marcus Liu: Grant CI access or coordinate Packer pipeline details if AMI required by 2026-02-06
Arun Patel: Schedule benchmark harness run in staging and share test plan by 2026-02-11
Sofia Alvarez: Record 2-minute demo video for marketplace listing and attach to package by 2026-02-08

Redwood to provide staging package (container image) + terraform module
Partner to run staging deploy and provide prompt set for bench tests
Run reconciliation and security questionnaire review
